title: Pneumonia with AKI, or something faster?
note: Fictional patient. Values are illustrative and follow the module’s KDIGO 2024 statements and grades; no doses are given. The unit’s protocol and the attending nephrologist decide every order.
intro:
You are the internal medicine resident admitting on the night shift at a government hospital in Iloilo City. Mr. Ramon Castillo, 63, a retired high school teacher, has had three weeks of fever, weight loss and aching joints. Twice this week he coughed up streaks of blood. Since yesterday his urine has been dark.

His creatinine was 1.1 mg/dL at a health check two months ago; it was 2.8 mg/dL on arrival this afternoon and 3.2 mg/dL now. The intern spun the urine and found dysmorphic red blood cells (RBCs) and red cell casts. The chest radiograph shows patchy shadows in both lungs. Hemoglobin is 9.8 g/dL. His wife finished tuberculosis treatment two years ago. The intern presents him as “community-acquired pneumonia with acute kidney injury (AKI).”

n1.prompt: What do you do in the next hour?

choices.text: Antibiotics for pneumonia; repeat the creatinine and urinalysis tomorrow.
choices.feedback: Red cell casts prove a glomerular source, and a creatinine rising by the hour with blood in the sputum is a pulmonary-renal syndrome until proven otherwise. Crescents scar within days to weeks, so tomorrow costs nephrons.
choices.then: At 23:00 the creatinine is higher again. You send the serologies and call the fellow and attending.

vitals.sero: Sent (send-out): ANCA, anti-GBM, C3, C4, ANA, anti-dsDNA

choices.text: Treat it as rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis (RPGN), possibly pulmonary-renal: send antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies (ANCA), anti-glomerular basement membrane (anti-GBM) antibody, C3, C4, antinuclear antibody (ANA) and anti-double-stranded DNA (anti-dsDNA) tonight, note the send-out time, and call the fellow and attending now.
choices.feedback: A nephritic urine with a creatinine higher than the last known value, plus hemoptysis, is the intern’s and resident’s trigger for same-day escalation. These tests sort RPGN into its three mechanisms, each with time-critical treatment.

vitals.sero: Sent (send-out): ANCA, anti-GBM, C3, C4, ANA, anti-dsDNA

choices.text: Send the serologies tonight and present him at morning rounds.
choices.feedback: The tests are right, but the call is not optional. Hemoptysis with a rising creatinine is on the module’s call-now list, and the attending may want treatment to start before results return.
choices.then: The nurse reports another streak of blood at 21:00. You call the fellow and attending.

vitals.sero: Sent (send-out): ANCA, anti-GBM, C3, C4, ANA, anti-dsDNA
MPO-ANCA positive; anti-GBM negative; C3, C4 normal

n2.scene: The reference laboratory phones: myeloperoxidase (MPO)-ANCA is positive; anti-GBM is negative and complement is normal. The earliest biopsy slot is Friday, and the immunofluorescence must be sent to Manila. The attending asks what you propose.

choices.text: Start the safety screen today (tuberculosis history and test, chest radiograph review, hepatitis B surface antigen and core antibody, hepatitis C, human immunodeficiency virus), and start immunosuppression with the attending without waiting for Friday’s biopsy.
choices.feedback: KDIGO 2024 states that with a compatible presentation and a positive MPO- or proteinase 3 (PR3)-ANCA, treatment should not be delayed for a biopsy, especially when the patient is deteriorating. His wife’s tuberculosis makes the screen urgent, not optional.

vitals.rx: Safety screen sent; induction planned before biopsy

choices.text: Wait for Friday’s biopsy before any treatment, so the diagnosis is certain.
choices.feedback: The crescent’s clock is running. A cellular crescent can still resolve; two more days of rising creatinine may turn it fibrous. The biopsy can follow when it is safe.
choices.then: The attending decides not to wait. The safety screen goes out this afternoon.

vitals.rx: Safety screen sent; induction planned before biopsy

choices.text: High-dose glucocorticoids and rituximab tonight; skip the screening because the disease is urgent.
choices.feedback: Latent tuberculosis can reactivate within weeks of immunosuppression, and his wife had it. Rituximab can reactivate hepatitis B into fulminant hepatitis. If treatment cannot wait, the screen still starts the same day, with a documented plan.
choices.then: The attending asks you to send the full safety screen first, today, and to document the plan.

vitals.rx: Safety screen sent; induction planned before biopsy

n3.prompt: Which initial regimen do you draft for the attending to review?

choices.text: A full-dose glucocorticoid taper with rituximab.
choices.feedback: Glucocorticoids with rituximab is a KDIGO 1B option. But in PEXIVAS a reduced-dose glucocorticoid schedule was noninferior and caused fewer serious infections at one year (incidence rate ratio 0.69), which matters with tuberculosis in the household.
choices.then: The attending switches to a reduced-dose glucocorticoid schedule.

choices.text: Glucocorticoids alone; add a second drug only if he does not respond.
choices.feedback: KDIGO 2024 recommends glucocorticoids in combination with cyclophosphamide or rituximab as initial treatment (1B). Waiting to see whether he responds lets crescents scar.
choices.then: The attending adds a second agent from the start.

choices.text: Glucocorticoids on a reduced-dose schedule with cyclophosphamide or rituximab, chosen with him and his family by cost and infection risk, with prophylaxis per protocol; note that avacopan may replace glucocorticoids where available.
choices.feedback: This is the 1B recommendation, delivered with the least glucocorticoid the evidence supports. In ADVOCATE, avacopan was noninferior to a prednisone taper at week 26. Most families pay for these drugs out of pocket, so write the cost conversation in the chart.

n4.scene: The nurse calls: he has coughed up a cupful of bright red blood. Oxygen saturation is 86% on room air. His hemoglobin has fallen to 8.1 g/dL, and a portable radiograph shows new shadows in both lungs.

choices.text: Furosemide for pulmonary edema, and review at morning rounds.
choices.feedback: Fresh hemoptysis, a falling hemoglobin and new infiltrates point to alveolar hemorrhage, not fluid. Waiting until morning in a hypoxemic patient can be fatal.
choices.then: His saturation falls further. You start oxygen and call the attending.

vitals.rx: Oxygen; attending called; plasma exchange transfer arranged

choices.text: Oxygen now, and discuss plasma exchange at rounds if he needs dialysis.
choices.feedback: Oxygen is right. But he already meets two KDIGO triggers for considering plasma exchange: alveolar hemorrhage with hypoxemia, and a creatinine above 3.4 mg/dL. Dialysis is not the threshold, and transfer takes time.
choices.then: At 05:00 you call the attending, who arranges transfer.

vitals.rx: Oxygen; attending called; plasma exchange transfer arranged

choices.text: Oxygen and airway support per protocol, and call the attending now: alveolar hemorrhage with hypoxemia and a creatinine above 3.4 mg/dL are where KDIGO says to consider plasma exchange. Start arranging transfer to a center that can do it.
choices.feedback: KDIGO 2024 practice point 9.3.1.9 names creatinine above 3.4 mg/dL, dialysis or a rapidly rising creatinine, and diffuse alveolar hemorrhage with hypoxemia. Plasma exchange is scarce outside large Philippine centers, so plan the transfer early.

vitals.rx: Oxygen; attending called; plasma exchange transfer arranged

choices.text: No plasma exchange: PEXIVAS showed it does not help.
choices.feedback: PEXIVAS found no significant benefit on death or kidney failure overall (28.4% versus 31.0%), with a wide confidence interval. That moved plasma exchange from routine to a considered option for the sickest, which is exactly where he is now.
choices.then: The attending, called at 04:00, arranges transfer for plasma exchange.

vitals.rx: Oxygen; attending called; plasma exchange transfer arranged

n5.scene: He came back from Manila after plasma exchange and is continuing induction therapy. The bleeding has stopped and his creatinine is falling. Today he has a fever of 38.6 °C and a new dry cough.

choices.text: Call the attending now and look for infection first, tuberculosis included, given his wife’s history, before any change in immunosuppression.
choices.feedback: Fever, a new cough or breathlessness in a patient on immunosuppression is on the module’s call list. In the Philippines, tuberculosis is a real risk: the country carried 6.8% of the world’s incident cases in 2024.

vitals.rx: Infection workup; attending deciding on immunosuppression

choices.text: Raise the glucocorticoid dose; this is a vasculitis flare.
choices.feedback: His kidney is improving and the bleeding has stopped. Fever and cough two weeks into induction are infection until proven otherwise, and more glucocorticoid would feed it.
choices.then: The attending declines and asks for an infection workup first.

vitals.rx: Infection workup; attending deciding on immunosuppression

choices.text: Start an empiric antibiotic and tell the attending at rounds.
choices.feedback: Treating infection is reasonable, but the attending needs to know today. The workup has to include tuberculosis, and the immunosuppression plan may change.
choices.then: The attending, told at rounds, widens the workup to include tuberculosis.

vitals.rx: Infection workup; attending deciding on immunosuppression

end.title: Month 3
end.text: The infection workup found a treatable chest infection, managed on the attending’s plan; tuberculosis testing was negative. He finished induction off dialysis, with his creatinine settling well above his old baseline. You documented the timeline, the send-out dates, the safety screen and the cost conversation, and the social worker connected the family with the Malasakit Center for his medicines.

debrief:
What this case teaches

  • A nephritic urine with a creatinine rising over days is RPGN until proven otherwise. Send ANCA, anti-GBM and complement today, and call.
  • Do not delay treatment for a biopsy when ANCA is positive and the patient is deteriorating, but start the tuberculosis and hepatitis B screen the same day.
  • Initial treatment is glucocorticoids with cyclophosphamide or rituximab (1B), with the least glucocorticoid the evidence supports.
  • Consider plasma exchange for the sickest: creatinine above 3.4 mg/dL, dialysis, or alveolar hemorrhage with hypoxemia. Plan transfer early.
  • Fever on immunosuppression means infection first, tuberculosis included.

See RPGN, ANCA and anti-GBM and Infection.
